title: I’m prototyping an AI-assisted interactive detective fiction app for Android — does this UI make the game feel playable?
author: CauliflowerLittle270
selftext:
Hi everyone, I’m an Android developer prototyping a mobile interactive detective fiction app.



The idea is not a normal visual novel or a chat-only story. Each story plays through a phone-like case system: you question suspects, collect evidence, inspect CCTV frames, build a timeline, and submit a final deduction.



This first story is called THE SEVENTH WITNESS.



Hook:

Six people claim innocence. The camera shows a seventh.



I’m still early, so this poster/UI mockup is mainly for testing the direction. I’m trying to figure out whether the concept reads as:



1. interactive detective fiction

2. a mobile mystery game

3. just a generic thriller poster



AI disclosure:

AI is being used for visual prototyping and early content iteration. The actual game structure is planned as a controlled story system rather than a freeform chatbot.



I’d love feedback from AI game devs:



Would this make you want to try a short 25–45 minute mobile mystery?

What would you expect the core interaction to be: interrogation, evidence matching, timeline solving, or final accusation?

Does the poster make the gameplay clear enough?

https://preview.redd.it/kq2t41mlgu7h1.png?width=1536&format=png&auto=webp&s=b1458e96ef04fc32e7e1c4be69f05e9563219e31

comments.author: AutomaticTalent
comments.body:
If this is a recreation of Clue! then no, the poster looks too complex.

Try developing the seed of the game play first - make it fun before adding all the AI icing.

AI can’t tell you if it’s beautiful, if it sounds good, or if it’s fun - you have to provide that.  And that’s the real work.
